svg.title: One orbit symbol, two bracket values
svg.desc: At the flat graph u=0 at the origin, X star equals x squared partial x plus x to the fourth partial u, and X zero equals x to the fourth partial u. Both have zero first jet and represent 24 partial u4. Bracketing with Y equals partial x plus x partial u gives different third-order values: X star retains minus 2 partial u2 and is not an order-three orbit symbol. The exact obstruction sequence below distinguishes full stabilizer lifting from first-derivative image lifting.

g.text: Same orbit symbol does not determine this bracket
Example 4.10 · N: u = 0 at (0,0) · k = 4 · Y = ∂x + x∂u
Entire third jet zero: sufficient here
X* − X₀ = x²∂x stabilizes every flat graph jet, but [Y, x²∂x]⁽³⁾ = −2∂u₂.
p: ordinary jet truncation; gₖ = ker p; Sᵢ = stabilizer; Aᵢ = action map.
Vanishing of the quotient supplies pure-symbol representatives, not a general theorem.
Original diagram · GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), Ultra · CC0-1.0 · See complete proofs in Section 4.10.
